 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, Advocate
 For the Opposite Party/s : Sri Amrendra Prasad, App
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajeev Ranjan Prasad
 Oral Order
2. 18-10-2017
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the State.

The petitioner, in the present case, is seeking anticipatory bail in connection with Kotwali P.S. Case No. 293 of 2017 for the offences under Sections 420, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act and Sections 57, 53, 50, 55 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, pending in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gaya.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the allegations are that of keeping palm oil and cream in the shop with the stove for the purpose of mixing the same with Ghee, but Annexure-2, the test report, has only shown the RM value being less than 28.0 which nowhere indicates that it is case of adulteration.
Learned counsel further submits that the test report is under challenge.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State opposes the prayer for bail of the petitioner and submits that the petitioner was found involved in selling adulterated Ghee and from his shop palm oil, cream and stoves were recovered which clearly shows that the petitioner was involved in mixing of undesired combinations and the same were being sold in the name of pure Ghee.
It is an offence in violation of Section 57 and 51 of the Food Safety and Standard Act.
It is further submitted that even blue kerosene oil has been seized from the possession of this petitioner.
The petitioner is apparently involved in selling of low quality of Ghee.
